experiences.title: Miku
experiences.summary: A teachable AI pupil that helps learners practise metacognitive calibration.

highlights.heading: What I built
highlights.body: The learner teaches Miku, an AI pupil that starts blank and answers only from what it has been taught. Before each question, the learner predicts whether Miku will get it right. The gap between prediction and result is the calibration measure.

highlights.heading: Where it came from
highlights.body: Two earlier versions, a reflection chatbot and a story-relay game, both aimed at helping children reflect on their own thinking.

highlights.heading: Where it stands
highlights.body: Adult friends have used it. I’m interviewing parents before any child does, so there is no child data and no claim that it works.

images.alt: Calibration map shown back to the learner
images.caption: Calibration map shown back to the learner

experiences.title: LSE, Department of Psychological and Behavioural Science
experiences.summary: Two separate research projects, each on a different question about how people judge what they know.

groups.heading: Dr Yana Litovsky
groups.note: Research apprenticeship · curiosity, guessing and misinformation
groups.body:
How guessing and processing fluency affect susceptibility to misleading claims.

It made me ask whether Miku’s prediction step anchors learners to their first judgement, which is a question about my design rather than a finding of hers.

groups.heading: Dr Sakshi Ghai
groups.note: Research assistantship · digital safety for young people in Kenya
groups.body:
I reviewed digital-safety interventions and mapped which might suit young people in Mukuru.

It made me rethink my first chatbot, which invited children to confide in an AI. An intervention can be coherent inside a framework and still miss how a community meets risk.

images.caption: Review notes or a mapping table from the Mukuru work

experiences.title: LinkSea
experiences.summary: Rebuilt the student interface of a school platform used every day at a middle school in Hong Kong.

highlights.heading: What I built
highlights.body: The student-facing interface, in JavaScript. The platform also has interfaces for teachers and administrators, which were not mine.

highlights.heading: How I tested it
highlights.body: With the students themselves. I rebuilt the parts they could not complete.

experiences.title: Noetic
experiences.summary: One-day builds where AI builders learn a frontier company’s newest tools with its engineers in the room.

highlights.heading: How a day is designed
highlights.body: Tracks are split by experience, so first-timers aren’t scored against people who have already shipped. Judges reward teams that can explain why they chose a model, ahead of how finished the build looks.

highlights.heading: The Nebius day
highlights.body: One day of several. 103 applicants, 63 selected, and all 63 came. Those are participation figures: they say who turned up, not what anyone learned.
